A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRUwE research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: V1 reports original forecasting, event-prediction and computational-efficiency experiments, including Tables 1–2 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and adds HyperIMTS comparisons and architectural-ablation results in Table 3.

M1.justification: GRUwE retains the same masked inputs, exponential time decay, GRU updates, shared transition/prediction basis, output functions and training objectives. The newly evaluated architectural variants are ablation controls, not revisions to the proposed model.

E1.justification: Both versions report forecasting on USHCN, Physionet and the two MIMIC-III datasets, and event prediction on Taxi, Retweet, StackOverflow and Amazon. V2's added comparisons and ablations reuse existing coverage; the online Physionet scenario is also retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds HyperIMTS to the forecasting comparison in Table 1 and the retrospective and online computational-cost comparisons. It reports accuracy on three datasets and OOM on MIMIC-III-Large. All previously evaluated baselines remain, and the event-prediction comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new ablation design introduces controls replacing the temporal basis, separating transition/prediction parameters, and freezing randomly initialized decay parameters. V2 also adds HyperIMTS-specific tuning configurations. Existing splits, preprocessing, metrics, retained-model training budgets and the 100-patient online evaluation protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: V1 has no architectural-ablation study. V2 adds Table 3 across all four forecasting datasets, testing linear versus sinusoidal versus exponential bases, shared versus separate exponential parameters, and learned versus frozen parameters. This substantially expands evidence about the contribution of GRUwE's central design choices.

E5.justification: V1 reports means and standard deviations over unspecified multiple random seeds; v2 specifies five seeds in Section 6 and Tables 1–2. This discloses the run count without establishing an increase in runs. The new ablation table reports point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive results about architectural choices in Table 3, plus HyperIMTS accuracy, OOM and computational-cost results. In Table 3, DualExp has lower USHCN MSE than GRUwE, 0.013 versus 0.014 in the reported ×10−2 scale, while GRUwE leads on the other three datasets. Original benchmark scores, event rankings and existing cost measurements remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The asymptotic analysis, Lipschitz theorem and proof, and growth/decay remark are retained. V1 Appendix 3 becomes v2 Appendix 1. The new latent-dynamics illustration and renamed subsection explain existing mathematics rather than introduce a new formal result.

C1.justification: The central claims of competitive accuracy, state-of-the-art forecasting on two datasets, highest overall event-prediction rank and efficient online inference remain. V2 narrows the introductory event-prediction comparison to RNN and attention methods, dropping v1's claim of matching or outperforming differential-equation TPP models.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations that exponential bases provide a useful temporal inductive bias, sharing parameters regularizes learning, and adapting decay rates benefits prediction. It also attributes HyperIMTS's MIMIC-III-Large memory failure to long sequences. The existing missingness interpretation and lack-of-uncertainty limitation remain.

D1.justification: V2 Appendices 3 and 5–8 add HyperIMTS's implementation source, hyperparameter search ranges, selected configurations and the smallest tested configuration that triggered OOM. Existing data-preparation instructions, retained-model hyperparameters and computing hardware are unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to HyperIMTS, Hi-Patch, LSTM and Liu and Hauskrecht's 2015 clinical time-series work, while removing Chen et al. (2020) and Liu and Hauskrecht (2019). It refines architectural comparisons, but much of the expanded main-text review already appeared in v1 Appendix 2.

P1.justification: V2 extensively revises the introduction, related work, model explanations, discussion and conclusion. It integrates the appendix literature review into the main text, introduces numbered sections and an appendix contents list, reorganizes appendix headings, adds acknowledgements and removes the generic broader-impact paragraph.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main text from a two-column layout to a single-column journal layout. It combines the problem and architecture diagrams into Figure 1, redraws the problem diagram, adds ablation Table 3 and latent-dynamics Figure 5, extends tables and cost plots with HyperIMTS, and revises result highlighting and captions.

improvement.justification: The ablations provide direct evidence for design choices that v1 supported mainly through explanation and benchmark comparisons. HyperIMTS evaluation, documented settings and explicit seed counts also strengthen the assessment. These gains are limited by missing ablation uncertainty estimates and interpretations that overgeneralize the shared basis's advantage despite DualExp's lower USHCN MSE.
